battle.title: Where Is That Domain?
battle.description: Chase a domain name from your laptop to the authoritative server.

questions.text: What does a recursive DNS resolver do for a client?
options: Stores the master copy of every zone it is asked about
Only returns a referral and leaves the client to follow it
Encrypts the connection between the client and the website
Performs the full lookup on its behalf and caches the answer
questions.answer: Performs the full lookup on its behalf and caches the answer
questions.explanation: The recursive resolver (often run by the ISP or a public DNS service) chases the answer through root, TLD and authoritative servers, then caches it. Authoritative servers hold the master records.

questions.text: Which DNS record type maps a hostname to an IPv4 address?
options: A
AAAA
MX
CNAME
questions.explanation: An A record holds an IPv4 address. AAAA holds IPv6, MX names the mail server and CNAME is an alias to another name.

questions.text: For an uncached name, which sequence matches how a recursive resolver finds the answer?
options: Authoritative server -> TLD server -> root server
TLD server -> root server -> authoritative server
Root server -> TLD server -> authoritative server
Root server -> authoritative server -> TLD server
questions.answer: Root server -> TLD server -> authoritative server
questions.explanation: The root points to the TLD servers (such as .com), the TLD servers point to the domain's authoritative servers, and those return the final record. Each step narrows the search.

questions.text: You will move your site to a new server IP next week. How do you minimise visitors hitting the old IP afterwards?
options: Raise the TTL so resolvers keep the record longer
Lower the record's TTL a few days before the move
Delete the A record on migration day and wait
Ask every user to flush their DNS cache
questions.answer: Lower the record's TTL a few days before the move
questions.explanation: Resolvers cache a record for its TTL, so a low TTL set in advance means stale copies expire quickly after you switch. A higher TTL prolongs the problem and you cannot flush other people's caches.

questions.text: A resolver follows CNAME aliases until it finds an address. What does this program print?
options: cdn.shop.test 1 10.1.1.1
www.shop.test 0 10.0.0.7
edge7.net.test 2 10.0.0.7
edge7.net.test 1 10.0.0.7
questions.explanation: The name www.shop.test is an alias of cdn.shop.test, which is an alias of edge7.net.test: two hops. Only then does an A record exist, giving 10.0.0.7. Resolvers restart the lookup on the target name, they do not stop at the alias.
